sections.skill: Recognize scope creep and handle changes with a change order

questions.prompt: What is scope creep?

choices.text: A supplier raising prices every year
Extra requests added without changing price or time
A customer paying an invoice a little early
A slow increase in the business's advertising budget

questions.correct_answer: Extra requests added without changing price or time
questions.intro: SCOPE is the work agreed in the quote or contract. SCOPE CREEP happens when extra requests keep being added without changing the price or timeline. Handle changes with a short CHANGE ORDER: a written note describing the new request, its added cost and time, approved by the customer before you start it. Small favors can be fine, but decide on purpose. Uncontrolled scope creep turns a profitable job into a loss.

sections.skill: Adding rooms to a house plan

questions.prompt: The third room is like what?
questions.correct_answer: A scope change
questions.intro: Imagine hiring a builder for a 2-room addition. Halfway through, you ask for a third room "while you're at it." A good builder writes down the extra room, its extra cost and extra time, and asks you to sign before starting. Without that note, the builder works for free or you get a surprise bill. A change order is that signed note.
